name: Parallel Processing Cortex Expansion
target_system: neural (corpus callosum and hemispheric independence enhancement)
description: Enhances the independence of the brain's two hemispheres while maintaining integrated consciousness, allowing genuine parallel processing of separate cognitive tasks. The user can hold two independent conversations simultaneously, read while listening, or solve two separate problems at once. This is not multitasking in the normal sense — it's two genuine cognitive threads running in parallel. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's installation includes enhanced corpus callosum bandwidth to prevent the hemispheres from desynchronizing. The modification is valued by analysts, traders, air traffic controllers, and anyone whose work requires monitoring multiple information streams simultaneously. The subjective experience is reportedly disorienting at first — users describe feeling like two people sharing one body — but adapts to a seamless sense of expanded awareness within 3–6 months.
source_organism: Octopus vulgaris (common octopus, distributed neural processing), synthetic hemispheric independence factors
procedure: Neural retroviral treatment targeting corpus callosum and hemispheric processing centers, 10 sessions over 6 months
side_effects: Hemispheric desynchronization episodes — the two 'threads' lose coherence, causing confusion, contradictory actions, or split-second paralysis
Each hemisphere may develop subtle personality differences over time
Dreams become double — users report experiencing two dreams simultaneously
Emotional regulation is complicated by competing hemispheric responses
Rare: permanent hemispheric split requiring pharmaceutical reunification
social_perception: Awe-inspiring and unsettling. People who can genuinely think two things at once are both admired and distrusted. The modification is rare enough that encountering a Split Brain user is noteworthy. Their ability to maintain two conversations simultaneously is uncanny to observe.
story_hooks: A Split Brain user's hemispheres begin disagreeing about a moral decision — one hemisphere wants to help, the other wants to run, and the body is caught between them

An intelligence agent's parallel processing allows them to decode a message while maintaining cover in a live conversation — but their split attention is detected by a scentreader who notices two distinct stress signatures from one person
